extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, activists, policymakers researching the #MeToo movement
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive encyclopedic overview of the #MeToo movement, its sectoral impacts (education, finance, Hollywood, tech, sports, etc.), policy responses, controversies, and criticisms. Summarizes events, investigations, proposed laws, industry reforms, and public debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ME TOO Congress Act — 180-day filing limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would ensure future complaints could only take up to 180 days to be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Member and Employee Training and Oversight on Congress Act (ME TOO Congress Act) as an amendment to the Congressional Accountability Act of 1995; framed as a reform to shorten delays in filing legislative-branch harassment complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: ME TOO Congress Act — staff transfer protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would allow staffers to transfer to a different department or otherwise work away from the presence of the alleged harasser without losing their jobs if they requested it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to give complainants practical options to avoid working with alleged harassers while preserving employment, instead of forcing continued exposure or resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ME TOO Congress Act — elected officials pay settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would require Representatives and Senators to pay for their harassment settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to remove the use of federal tax funds to pay settlements and increase accountability for lawmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ME TOO Congress Act — public disclosure of settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Compliance would no longer be allowed to keep settlements secret and would be required to publicly publish the settlement amounts and the associated employing offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transparency measure to discourage secretive settlements and allow public scrutiny of where settlement funds were spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: ME TOO Congress Act — protections for unpaid workers
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first time, the same protections would also apply to unpaid workers, including pages, fellows and interns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends harassment protections beyond paid staff to prevent exploitation of unpaid/trainee roles in the legislative branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of prior Office of Compliance confidentiality process
rubrics_metrics.description: The old system channeled complaints through the Office of Compliance, which required complete confidentiality through the process and took months of counseling and mediation before a complaint could be filed; settlement payments were paid using federal taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural arrangement was criticized as delaying redress, silencing complainants, and hiding settlement costs from public view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to cut federal research funding for proven harassers (MeTooSTEM)
rubrics_metrics.description: BethAnn McLaughlin called for the National Institutes of Health to cut funding to anyone who has been found guilty of harassment charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed sanction linking research funding eligibility to findings of harassment; part of broader efforts to use funding as leverage to enforce professional conduct in STEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional investigation and consequences for substantiated harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantiated reports of sexual harassment have led to removal of names from buildings/programs, resignations, and reprimands (e.g., Francisco J. Ayala name removal; Ron Carlson resignation after substantiated reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 97-page internal UC Irvine report compiled testimony and resulted in removal of endowments/names and personnel actions—illustrates that thorough investigations and documented testimony can prompt institutional sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate disclosure of diversity statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been pressure on companies, specifically in the financial industry, to disclose diversity statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is framed as a transparency/accountability practice intended to highlight representation gaps and inform corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of gender-exclusive, demeaning event practices (Presidents Club example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that exclude women except as 'hostesses' and subject them to demeaning rules prompted shutdowns (The Presidents Club was shut down after undercover reporting documented widespread sexual misconduct and exclusionary rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undercover journalism exposed practices that led to reputational and operational consequences; demonstrates that exclusionary event policies can be grounds for public condemnation and cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform of NDAs and employment-contract provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: There have been bans on nondisclosure agreements in some states and changes to employment contracts with regards to NDAs and laws in Washington and California, in response to #MeToo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy reforms aim to prevent NDAs being used to silence victims; states have moved to restrict or ban NDAs in sexual harassment/assault settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform incident response and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms should investigate credible reports, create incident response teams, and take action such as bans (e.g., Twitch created an incident response team 'Gold Sparrow'; Dr Disrespect received a lifetime ban).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies and platforms are expected to establish processes for promptly handling credible harassment allegations and to enforce community/employee standards, including removal or bans when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove forced arbitration clauses from employment contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees walked out demanding the removal of forced arbitration clauses from employment contracts after harassment allegations (Riot Games example).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing forced arbitration is promoted as a mechanism to allow employees access to public legal remedies and class actions rather than private arbitration that may limit accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companies must maintain adequate procedures for misconduct complaints and respect whistleblower protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC fined Activision Blizzard for failure to maintain adequate procedures for employee misconduct complaints and for violating a whistleblower law by requiring employees to notify the company if they receive a request for information from an investigative body like the SEC or the NLRB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firms are required to have robust internal complaint procedures and cannot circumvent external investigative processes or intimidate potential whistleblowers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military prosecution reform (Military Justice Improvement Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Military Justice Improvement Act would move 'the decision over whether to prosecute serious [sex] crimes to independent, trained, professional military prosecutors, while leaving uniquely military crimes within the chain of command'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal aims to reduce command influence and improve impartiality in prosecuting military sexual offenses by transferring charging decisions to independent prosecutors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections and reforms for pornographic performers
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for the industry to police itself better: mandating training courses that teach performers their rights, providing access to independent hotlines where performers can report abuse, and discussions about raising the legal age of entry into adult entertainment from 18 to 21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates argue for measures that improve safety, reduce stigma, and provide reporting/support mechanisms for performers rather than criminalizing the industry; opponents warn restricting porn could harm performers' autonomy and livelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive sex education to prepare youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Several feminists argue it is crucial to provide children with basic sex education before exposure to pornography, to prepare children to identify and say no to unwanted sexual contact and to teach about consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned as a preventative/educational policy complementing other reforms; cites studies linking abstinence-only education to worse outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical context on false allegations and due process concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion that false reports make up a small percentage of total reports, with figures from DOJ and other organizations finding around 2–10% of rape and sexual assault allegations reported to police are determined to be false after thorough investigation. A UK Home Office study was cited with related data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in debates to argue for balancing support for victims (#BelieveWomen) with respect for due process; commentators emphasize that belief in victims does not preclude due process protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severing commercial ties and removing content in response to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Media companies, platforms, and brands have removed content or severed ties with accused individuals (examples: radio stations removing 'Baby, It's Cold Outside'; Spotify removing artists from curated playlists; Peloton removing Diddy's music; brands ending partnerships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial decisions are often used as sanctions or reputational responses while legal processes continue; platforms sometimes modify content policies (Spotify's 'hateful conduct' policy and later rollback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accountability in sports and other fields following mass allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: When many victims come forward, prosecutions and institutional leadership consequences can follow (e.g., Larry Nassar's convictions, Michigan State University president resignation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates that collective disclosures can prompt criminal investigations, civil lawsuits, and leadership resignations/organizational change.

rubrics_metrics.name: High prevalence and underreporting in medical and academic fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Research indicates among U.S. academic medical faculty around 30% of women and 4% of men reported experiencing sexual harassment; many medical trainees/students experienced harassment during training but most do not report incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights need for systemic changes in reporting mechanisms, career protections for complainants, and cultural reform to reduce retaliation and career harm from reporting.
